decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY that makes the legacy power-board connector constraints inapplicable and removes the obsolete placement and access keys.
General connector-placement flexibility remains subject to the antenna orientation and keepout constraints specified immediately before the source message.
The source relies on the already-established single-board topology but does not change the architecture or board count.
Connector placement on the available board sides does not alter the cost goal, component-selection policy, integrated architecture, or elimination of interboard connectors.
The source permits flexible physical placement but does not change the required sensor connector fanout, connector types, individual-cable policy, or elimination of interboard connectors.
The source changes only general connector placement; the USB interface, sourceability, and programming-port role remain unchanged.
Connector-side flexibility does not change I2C speed, pull-ups, series resistors, topology, or their integrated-board location.
The source concerns connector placement on the integrated board and does not change the legacy main-board BOM or optional connector population decision.
The source does not alter any battery electrical-protection controller, cutoff, or protection-component requirement.
The reference to easily positioned LEDs concerns layout flexibility and does not change the e-paper backlight circuit, supply, control, or required position behind the display.
The breakout already permits placement anywhere on the board, and the source does not change its pin coverage, through-hole style, pitch, or reuse purpose.
Permitting connectors on any of the proposed sides does not change the decision to use through-hole connectors throughout the current design.
